hypothesis_or_artifact: Scope limit 2 -- that the four cases were not sampled from a population -- and the absence of any multiplicity or selection correction on the cross-experiment conclusion.
label: READ
claim_quote:
2. **Four cases are four cases.** They were not sampled from a population of
   hypotheses; they are the hypotheses one operator happened to run in a
   five-week window.
evidence_summary: The population is asserted, never exhibited. The case set was supplied, not enumerated: 'The governing instruction named seven repositories to read in full and read-only' (progress.md:22-24), corroborated by tests/test_sources.py:41-42 ('The note was commissioned against seven repositories. All seven are cited.'); n = 7 supplied repositories, 8 with AiTrader (progress.md:47-50). Nothing establishes that those seven are all the hypotheses run in the stated five-week window. The unit of analysis also changes between numerator and denominator: each power case is one repository carrying one hypothesis, while MLCryptoEngine as a single contrast case carries 'Eleven hypotheses, nine tested and closed, and not one closed on power' (SOURCES.md:168) -- so per hypothesis the corpus is 4 power closures against at least 11 non-power closures, not 4 against 3. The count is frozen by tests/test_cases.py:30-32 ('assert len(POWER_CASES) == 4'). Meanwhile the one thresholded negative whose verdict rested on a z bar received a multiplicity correction ('a corrected bar of 2.50', SOURCES.md:134) while the cross-experiment conclusion receives none.
recomputation: scratchpad/work/agentB-rpl/recompute.py, inputs z bar 2.50 and z realized 1.668 from SOURCES.md:134 (n = 1 holdout of 2.55 years). Two-sided p at z = 2.50 is 0.01242, i.e. alpha = 0.05/4.03; the Bonferroni m = 4 critical value at alpha = 0.05 is z = 2.4977, so the 'corrected bar of 2.50' is consistent with a family of four to two decimals. For completeness z = 1.668 gives two-sided p = 0.09532, so that negative also fails an uncorrected 1.96 bar and the correction did not decide it. The inference is about the standard applied to one case versus the standard applied to the cross-case conclusion.
would_resolve: An enumeration in the repository of the hypotheses run in the stated five-week window with the inclusion rule stated; or a restatement of scope item 2 as 'four cases drawn from seven repositories supplied by the commissioning instruction'; or a per-hypothesis count in the contrast comparison.
confidence_why: The supplied-set fact and the unit mismatch are documented inside this repository and are firm, but whether further hypotheses existed in the window can only be settled against the other repositories in the program; and the Bonferroni identification of the 2.50 bar is an inference from arithmetic, not a quotation.
invalidation_note: No for this repository -- dda39b2 is the branch tip. The population half could be re-opened by evidence from sibling repositories, which is why confidence is MEDIUM.

hypothesis_or_artifact: The headline conclusion -- that in all four cases the binding constraint was achievable sample size -- as applied to InsiderExperiment.
label: READ
claim_quote:
**Across four independent pre-registered experiments, the binding constraint was
not whether a published effect exists but whether an achievable sample could
detect an effect of the reported size.**
evidence_summary: Every sample-size input for InsiderExperiment cleared its registered bar by the repository's own record: '4,585 qualifying events against a registered floor of 1,000; 2,581 sessions at 99.5 percent coverage against a floor of 80 percent; 2,869.9 effective independent periods' (SOURCES.md:74; identical string at rplimits/cases.py:151-156). The repository states outright that sample size was not the binding term -- 'Sample required. Not a sample requirement.' and 'The 9.993 percent annualized tracking error is the whole of the 49.35' (SOURCES.md:78, n = 71.9 names behaving as 29.7 effective). A pre-registered variant on the identical sample would have cleared the bar: 'The equal-weighted secondary, on the identical 71.9 names, would have landed at 34.29 bp and fired DEGRADED' (docs/the-power-limit.md:227-229). 34.29 sits below the registered BLOCKED floor of 40 (SOURCES.md:70), inside the gross band 30-40 and below the top of the net band 13.3-34.7 (SOURCES.md:66). The cited closing commit subject says the same: 'Close at BLOCKED on the power gate, weight concentration not corpus, artifacts preserved' (rplimits/sources.py:100; SOURCES.md:222). The limitation is disclosed by the authors, so this is capped at S3 and labelled READ; what remains is that neither README.md:3-5 nor the note's claim section (docs/the-power-limit.md:11-19) carries it, and 'Not a sample requirement' appears 0 times in README.md.
recomputation: scratchpad/work/agentB-rpl/recompute.py. Inputs: 4,585 events and floor 1,000 (SOURCES.md:74); 34.29 bp (docs/the-power-limit.md:228); BLOCKED floor 40 and bands 30-40 / 13.3-34.7 (SOURCES.md:70, :66); 2,581 sessions and N_eff 2,869.9 (SOURCES.md:74). Results: 4,585/1,000 = 4.585x the corpus floor; 2,581/2,869.9 = 0.89933, matching the stated variance inflation 0.899 (a deflation, VIF < 1); 34.29 < 40 (BLOCKED floor), 34.29 < 34.7 (top of the net band), 34.29 inside 30-40 (gross band). No sample-size quantity in this case failed any bar.
would_resolve: Either restating the headline as three cases plus one portfolio-construction closure, or carrying 'Not a sample requirement' into README.md where the headline lives; or evidence from InsiderExperiment/REGISTRATION.md that the value-weighted primary was itself forced by an achievable-sample constraint rather than chosen (which requires the sibling repository and belongs to the cross-repository pass).

The 9.993 percent annualized tracking error is the whole of the 49.35.') and retail-power-limits/docs/the-power-limit.md:386-389 ('InsiderExperiment is the clearest instance: its verdict turned entirely on tracking error, and its own equal-weighted secondary on the identical names would have landed at 34.29 bp instead of 49.35.').
